Find the area bounded between the curve $x={y}^{2}+2y,$ the $y$-axis, and the lines $y=0$ and $y=-2,$ as shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}({y}^{2}+2y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y+2{\int }_{-2}^{0}y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}|}_{-2}^{0}+2\cdot {\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}|}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =(0-\frac{(-2)^{3}}{3})+2(0-\frac{(-2)^{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{8}{3}-4 \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies to the left of the $y$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is $|-\frac{4}{3}|=\frac{4}{3}.$
